transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because my brain feels like it just… stalls out. Like at work, I’ll have a test report open, or even something simple like a CAD note, and I’ll just sit there for an hour not knowing what the next sentence or checkbox should be. It’s embarrassing because it shouldn’t be hard, you know? I used to be able to just move through that stuff. Now I kind of get stuck staring at it, and then I start thinking about how everyone else probably already finished their part, and—sorry, I’m getting off track. That’s the main thing. I can’t think clearly enough to do basic work tasks.
How often do you feel like your brain stalls out like this? Is it most days, and does it last throughout the day?

Yeah… it happens a lot at work. I don’t know if I’d say every single minute of the day, but most days I’ll have something open—like a test report or even just a small CAD note—and I just sit there. Like, I can’t figure out the next sentence or even which checkbox makes sense, and then suddenly an hour has gone by.

It’s not like I’m doing something complicated, either. That’s what bothers me. I used to be pretty good at that kind of thing. I’ll try to start, then I’ll think about how behind I’m getting, or how everyone else probably just does it without thinking, and then I’m even more stuck. So… yeah, most days, and it can take up a big chunk of the day when it starts happening.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling like you're not good enough or letting people down?

Yeah… I guess losing interest, mostly. Like, I have this little 3D printer for miniatures, and there’s been the same half-finished figure sitting there for months. I keep seeing it and thinking I should just finish it, it wouldn’t even take that long, but then I don’t.

And stuff that used to help, like yoga or going for a walk in the woods, now it just feels like another chore on the list. Like I’m supposed to do it because it’s “good for me,” not because I actually want to. Which is weird, because I used to really like that kind of thing.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or that you’re letting people down, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yeah… I do. I keep replaying these tiny mistakes from the lab, like a number I should’ve double-checked or a note I worded awkwardly, and it just turns into this whole thing in my head.

It’s not even just “I messed up at work.” It starts feeling like I’m bad at the job, and then somehow that turns into… I’m bad as a person. Like if there are consequences, I deserve them. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, but that’s where my mind goes.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like your 3D printing or going for walks, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore?

Yeah… that’s pretty much it. The 3D printer thing is the clearest example, I guess. I have the same little miniature sitting there half-done, and it’s been months. I keep meaning to finish it, and then I just… don’t.

And walks too. I used to like being in the woods, like noticing the trail or whatever, but now it feels more like I’m checking off something I’m supposed to do. Same with yoga. It’s not relaxing exactly—it’s more like another task.
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble functioning like this before?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had stressful stretches before, like in school when everything piled up and I’d get kind of shut down for a bit, but I don’t know if it was the same as this.

It’s hard to compare, because back then I could sort of blame exams or deadlines or whatever. Like there was always a clear reason. This feels… I don’t know. I’m not sure I can say there was another period exactly like this.
Have you ever had a time before this where you felt down or lost interest in things for a period of time, even when there wasn’t a clear reason like school stress or a big deadline?

I don’t really know. I keep trying to think of an example, but then I start comparing it to school or work stuff, and it gets messy.

Like in college there were weeks where I’d just kind of go quiet and stop doing much besides what I had to do, but there was always some obvious reason, like a project or exams. And even now I’m wondering if I’m remembering it wrong because I used to be so bad at keeping track of time—like I’d tell myself something was “a couple weeks” and it was actually two days or two months.

So… I’m not sure. I can’t point to a time before this where it happened for no reason.

Can you think of any time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than a couple of weeks, even when things weren’t particularly stressful or there wasn’t a big deadline or event going on?

I’m trying to think… but I honestly can’t pin one down. Like, there were times where I was down for a while, but then I start remembering, oh, that was when I had a lab due, or I was waiting on feedback from a supervisor, or there was some family thing in the background.

And I’m bad at separating it, because even when nothing “big” was happening, I’d still make things stressful somehow—like I’d procrastinate on laundry or emails and then that became the event, if that makes sense.

So… no, I don’t think I can say there was a time like that for more than a couple weeks when nothing was really going on. I’m not sure.
How long has this been going on—this feeling of your brain stalling out, losing interest in things, and being hard on yourself?

I think it started around when they moved me into the prototype-testing role… so, about a year and a month ago? It’s hard to say exactly because at first I kept thinking it was just the new job, like I wasn’t used to the workflow or the equipment setup, and I was comparing it to my old tasks too much.

But yeah… if I’m being honest, it’s been going on since then. Around thirteen months, I guess.
Can you think of a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, even when there wasn’t anything particularly stressful going on?

I’m sorry, I know I keep circling this, but I really can’t think of one clearly. I can remember random stretches where I was kind of flat or not doing much, but then I start attaching them to something—classes, work, some deadline, some awkward thing with people—and then I don’t know if it counts.

It’s like when I try to sort my memories by “stressful” and “not stressful,” they don’t stay in the right boxes. So before this current stretch… I don’t think I can say yes. I’m not sure.
Can you recall having more than one separate time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things, with periods of feeling better in between those times?

I don’t know… I’m trying to line them up like separate “episodes,” but it gets messy in my head. Like, I can remember being better at certain points, or at least more normal, but then I also remember being stressed about something around those times, so I don’t know if it was really a separate thing or just life being uneven.

I had this notebook once where I tried to track moods, but then I started using it for grocery lists and work notes, so that didn’t really help. Sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess the answer is… I can’t clearly recall more than one separate time like that. Not in a way I’d feel confident saying yes.

Can you think of more than one separate time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things, where each time was clearly distinct from each other and not just part of one long ongoing period?

I don’t think I can separate it that cleanly. Like, I keep trying to make a timeline in my head, but then it sort of blurs together, and I start remembering random things that were happening around the same time—work stuff, people stuff, just… life—and then I’m not sure if those were separate periods or just the same kind of low feeling continuing underneath.

So… more than one clearly distinct time? I can’t really say that. I don’t have a clear example of that.
Can you think of more than one separate time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things, where each time was clearly distinct from the others and not just part of one ongoing period?

I know you’re asking if there were separate, clear times, like one ended and then another one started later. I’m trying to answer that, but I keep thinking about how I’d organize old photos on my phone and then get distracted by the dates being wrong, or like one folder has work screenshots mixed in with pictures of my cat, and then I lose the thread.

So… no, I can’t really give you more than one clearly separate time. It doesn’t feel clean enough in my memory for me to say that. I just don’t know.
Can you think of more than one separate time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things, where each time was clearly distinct from the others and not just part of one ongoing period?

I’m sorry, I know I keep circling this. I just… I don’t have a neat answer. When I try to think of it as separate chunks, I start thinking about where I was living, what job I had, whether it was before or after I changed phones—because I lost a bunch of old messages when I did that—and then I’m not actually answering you.

So, no, I can’t really think of more than one clearly separate time like that. It feels more blurred together than that, at least in my memory.
